title: Majestic Style
reviewNotes: Reconstructed six-piece position after ...Rg2. Four checked branches: pinned-rook diversion, direct queen mate, two illustrated replies after deliberate queen promotion, and drawing immediate promotion. g8=Q+ gives check in both sacrifice and immediate-promotion lines; diversion matters because ...Rxg8 is no longer available. Earlier king retreat is context.
transcript: Chess is a game of style, but when push comes to shove, will you choose precision or majesticness? It seems like this game is going to fizzle out to a draw, but actually this white to move and after pawn to G7 white is threatening to get a new queen on the next move. He can indeed start to give checks to the king like this and if white tries to go to E5 and stop the checks by walking towards the rook, actually the rook is not going to give checks anymore and play to G6 behind the pawn. What? Can't white just promote? Well, of course, but after black recaptures and white recaptures, believe it or not this position is actually a draw. There is no way for the white rook to collect the black pawn without sacrificing itself. The king is too far away to intervene and this would still be a draw. So, going back to the initial position, we need to realize that after the rook check, white has to go down and after black gives more checks, we need to keep going down with the king. Black checks us and we go down. Black checks us and we go down. But now actually things have changed for white because believe it or not the king can now go to E3. What? Weren't we trying to avoid this? Well, let's first of all see what happens if black continues to give checks. The king is going to walk towards the rook and if the rook goes to G3, this time the king is close enough. We can promote and after we win the rook, the rook is going to come around and with the help of the king, we are going to be able to [music] win against this king. Okay, so clearly black cannot allow white to get one step closer with that king and instead he's going to run behind the pawn with rook to G2 and this time promoting [music] is not good enough. The white king is still one step too far. So, white has to come up with another brilliant resource. The majestic rook to H2. The rook is pinned to the king. He has to take the white rook, but now this will allow white to promote with a check. If the king goes down, this is just going to be a fork picking up the rook. But if the king comes outside to B2, we now have to give a fork on B8 and pick up the rook like this. [music] And this is slightly more tricky because black is going to push the pawn and now be only one square away from promotion. You see, white has two different ways of winning this game. The first one is to play king to D3. And after king to B1, only move, instead of allowing black to promote, we can play queen to C2 check. King A1 and queen C1 checkmate. But who would do that when the alternative is so stylish? We can play king to C3, allow black to promote with a check, which seems crazy, but actually, after king to B3, we are placing black in a zugzwang. This black queen has no safe checks that it can give to the king. All of these squares are covered by our queen, which means that no matter what black plays, we are going to deliver a checkmate on B2 or on C2 and win this game in style.
